Assume Countable Choice. Let $B=[0,1]^d$, where $d$ is finite, and let $j_{b,s}$ be a smooth family of orientation-compatible complex structures on a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$, for $(b,s)\in B\times[0,1]$. Smoothness at the boundary means local smooth extendibility. For every $m\ge1$, the relative symmetric products $X_{b,s}=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma,j_{b,s})$ admit a smooth coefficient atlas over $B\times[0,1]$, with smooth vertical complex structure. There are diffeomorphisms
$$\Phi_{b,s}:X_{b,0}\longrightarrow X_{b,s},\qquad \Phi_{b,0}=I,$$
smooth jointly in all variables in that relative atlas, and genuine smooth permutation-equivariant ordered lifts on $\Sigma^m$. Both the maps and their inverses have bounded derivatives of each fixed order on the compact parameter-product spaces. They preserve every multiplicity stratum and every chosen finite point-incidence divisor, and their ordered lifts preserve each pairwise diagonal and each coordinate incidence set.

As in the one-parameter construction, the maps may be the raw identity near any fixed compact off-diagonal subset avoiding the prescribed point divisors, for example the union of two product tori. If the structures are independent of $s$ on a fixed spatial region, given smooth $b$-dependent holomorphic charts there may be retained unchanged in $s$, and the transport may be the raw identity on a smaller such region. Prescribed constant charts may likewise be retained unchanged wherever the whole family is already fixed. All simultaneous prescriptions must agree on their overlaps. If the entire surface family is independent of $s$ on a parameter-end collar, the horizontal field can be the raw constant-point field on that collar, so the transport is constant in $s$ there. This does not assert that its value on the terminal collar is the identity.

These are actual smooth finite-parameter transports, including parameter squares used for homotopies. No extension of an arbitrarily prescribed trivialization on the entire boundary of a parameter cube is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual complete pointed closed Heegaard diagram, a positive surface area form $\eta$, and one point $q_R$ in each complementary region, including its basepoint $z$. Let $j_a$ be a smooth compact finite-parameter family of positive surface structures and let $X_a=\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma,j_a)$. Supply actual smooth relative transports $\Phi_a:X_*\to X_a$ with smooth equivariant ordered lifts, preserving the discriminant and every $E_{q_R}$, raw-identity near both tori and common exact generator charts. Such families may be constructed by the finite-parameter transport lemma along prescribed paths from a fixed reference parameter. No arbitrary boundary trivialization is presumed.

Let $a(s)$ be a smooth profile constant at both source ends. On $X_*$ consider an actual smooth finite-energy fixed-end solution
$$u_s+K_{s,t}(u)u_t=W_s(u),\qquad u(s,0)\in L_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in L_\beta.$$
Here $W$ is smooth, independent of $t$, compactly supported in $s$, zero near both tori and the common generator charts, and has a smooth permutation-equivariant ordered lift preserving all pairwise diagonals and coordinate incidence sets. The physical vertical structures $(\Phi_{a(s)})_*K_{s,t}$ equal $\operatorname{Sym}^g(j_{a(s)})$ near the protected discriminant and incidence divisors, tame the descended fixed product area form elsewhere, and have the stated common fixed full boundary structure and generator charts. Take uniform smooth bounds and taming constants on the actual compact parameter families under consideration. Uniform generator limits at both ends are required.

Every region multiplicity is nonnegative. There is a finite smooth branched ordered cover of the strip, and
$$E(u)\le C\left(\sum_R n_R(u)\operatorname{Area}_\eta(R)+\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(|a'(s)|^2+\|\widetilde W_s\|_\infty^2\bigr)\,ds\right),$$
where $\widetilde W$ is the supplied ordered lift and $C$ is uniform on the stated compact families. If the fixed diagram is globally weakly admissible and $n_z=0$, only finitely many such integral domains occur across all endpoint pairs, without an index restriction; consequently these actual solutions have a uniform energy bound whenever the displayed forcing integral is uniformly bounded. Genus zero is the one-point case. No map counts, relative grading or invariance conclusion is included.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth family of almost complex structures on $X$, defined for $(s,t)$ in an open subset $U\subset\mathbb R^2$. Suppose the norms of $J$ and its derivatives through total order two, using the Levi-Civita connection in $X$ and ordinary derivatives in $s,t$, are uniformly bounded. Then there are constants $a,b\ge0$, depending only on these bounds and $g$, such that every smooth solution
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$$
has energy density $e=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$ satisfying
$$\Delta e\ge-ae^2-be.$$
Consequently there are $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the same data such that, whenever $\overline B_r(z)\subset U$, $0<r\le r_0$, and $\int_{B_r(z)}e<\varepsilon_0$, one has
$$|du(z)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{3\pi r^2}\int_{B_r(z)}e.$$
These are interior estimates for smooth actual solutions. No boundary estimate or higher-derivative compactness is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, with a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, and let $L\subset X$ be a compact embedded submanifold without boundary of half its real dimension. Let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth uniformly $C^2$ bounded family of almost complex structures for parameters in a neighborhood of a closed upper half-disk. Suppose $J(s,0,x)=J_b(x)$ for $x\in L$, independently of $s$, where $TL\cap J_bTL=0$.

There is a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on $X$, depending only on $g_0,L,J_b$, such that $J_b$ is orthogonal and $J_bTL$ is perpendicular to $TL$ along $L$. For this metric there are constants $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the geometric data and uniform family bounds with the following property. If $0<r\le r_0$ and a smooth map $u:\overline B_r^+\to X$ solves $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$, maps the flat edge into $L$, and satisfies $E=\int_{B_r^+}e_g<\varepsilon_0$, then
$$|du(0,0)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{\pi r^2}E,\qquad \sup_{B_{r/2}^+}|du|_g^2\le\frac{128}{\pi r^2}E,$$
where $e_g=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$. Uniformly equivalent estimates with constants depending on the data hold for $g_0$. No assumption that the whole image lies in one coordinate chart is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $G$ be the unit disk in $\mathbb R^2$ or its upper half-disk. Let $Q\subset\mathbb C^m$ be compact and let $J(s,t,x)$ be smooth on a neighborhood of $\overline G\times Q$, with $J^2=-I$ and uniform bounds on derivatives of every order. Suppose a smooth map $u:\overline G\to Q$ satisfies
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0,\qquad \sup_G(|u|+|du|)\le M,\qquad \sup_G\|J(s,t,u)-i\|\le\frac12.$$
In the half-disk case additionally suppose $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$. Then for each $0<\rho<1$ and integer $k\ge0$ there is a uniform bound
$$\|u\|_{H^k(G\cap B_\rho)}+\sup_{G\cap B_\rho}|D^ku|\le C_k.$$
The constants depend only on $m,M,\rho,k$ and finitely many of the indicated coefficient bounds. The estimates apply to already smooth solutions; they do not assert weak-solution regularity.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $G$ be a disk or an upper half-disk in $\mathbb R^2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^{2m}$ be open, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be smooth, including the straight source boundary in the half-disk case, with $J^2=-I$. Let $u:G\to\Omega$ be continuous, belong locally to $W^{1,2}$, and satisfy
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$$
weakly. In the half-disk case assume continuity and local $W^{1,2}$ also up to the straight boundary, $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m\subset\mathbb C^m=\mathbb R^{2m}$, and $\mathbb R^m\cap J(s,0,u(s,0))\mathbb R^m=\{0\}$. Then $u$ is smooth locally, including all one-sided derivatives at the straight boundary. Thus a continuous $W^{1,2}$ weak solution in smooth target charts with a flattened totally real boundary has classical smooth regularity. Continuity at a missing puncture is a premise, not a conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse totally real boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$ with finite intersection $K$, and smooth families $J_{n,t}$ converging smoothly to $J_{\infty,t}$. Their boundary structures on $L_0,L_1$ are fixed independently of $n$. Assume all these structures are exactly $i$ on common disjoint product generator charts taking $L_0,L_1$ to transverse product real lines, as in the actual transverse-strip neck lemma. Let smooth finite-energy solutions
$$\partial_su_n+J_{n,t}(u_n)\partial_tu_n=0,\qquad u_n(s,j)\in L_j,$$
on $\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ have energies at most $E_0$.

After a subsequence, either all maps are one constant generator, or there are finitely many longitudinal translations $q_{1,n}<\cdots<q_{M,n}$ with $q_{j+1,n}-q_{j,n}\to\infty$ and finitely many bubbled strip levels. Each level consists of a finite-energy $J_{\infty,t}$ strip, possibly constant, with finite sphere/disk bubble trees at its interior or physical boundary points. These are the actual local rescaling limits, have equal component values at their nodes, and constant bubbles satisfy the usual sphere node count or weighted disk node count. Each level has positive energy when its bubbles are included. The translated maps converge smoothly locally off the bubble points, including boundary derivatives, and all bubbles are smooth rescaled limits off their children.

After fixing the original end generators by a subsequence, adjacent strip levels have equal intermediate end generators, the first negative end and last positive end are the original ones, and
$$\lim_nE_g(u_n)=\sum_{j=1}^M\left(E_g(v_j)+\sum_{w\text{ on level }j}E_g(u_w)\right).$$
There is no energy or image diameter left between successive level cores or outside the first and last cores as their radii tend to infinity after the sequence limit. The number of levels and bubble components is uniformly bounded in terms of $E_0$ and the fixed geometric data. No exclusion of bubbles, index bound, regularity, or gluing is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$ having finite transverse intersection $K$. Let $J_t$ be smooth, independent of the longitudinal variable, with fixed boundary structures on $L_0,L_1$. Suppose there are disjoint generator charts about $K$ in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=\prod_j e^{i\theta_j(x)}\mathbb R$, $0<\theta_j(x)<\pi$, and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Such actual auxiliary choices exist in the product-torus setting by the generator-neighborhood lemma.

There are constants $\delta_0,c,C>0$ such that the following holds. Let $u$ be a smooth solution on $[a-1,b+1]\times[0,1]$ with these boundary conditions, and suppose every window $[s-1/2,s+1/2]\times[0,1]$, $s\in[a,b]$, has energy at most $\delta\le\delta_0$. Then the image of $[a,b]\times[0,1]$ lies in one of the generator charts. For $1\le R\le(b-a)/2$,
$$E_g(u;[a+R,b-R]\times[0,1])\le C\delta e^{-cR},$$
and its image has diameter at most $C\sqrt\delta e^{-cR/2}$ and lies within that distance of that chart's generator. The constants are independent of neck length. The same bounds hold on a semi-infinite neck, measuring distance from its finite end.

Every actual nonconstant finite-energy strip on $\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ with these fixed data has energy at least $\delta_0$, after possibly decreasing that constant. No regularity, index, or gluing theorem is presupposed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and let $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with standard complex structure $J_0$, quotient $q:\Sigma^m\to X$, and repeated-point locus $\Delta$. Off $\Delta$, the product form $\Omega=\sum_l\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$ descends to $\omega$. Fix a smooth target metric $g$ and finitely many attaching curves with finitely many complementary regions $R$. A product torus $L_\gamma$ uses one point on each of a labeled system of $m$ pairwise disjoint curves $\gamma_i$ among those curves. Choose a point $a_R$ in each region. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a fixed neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and on a fixed neighborhood of every $E_{a_R}=\{a_R\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$.

Let $u$ be a smooth $J_\tau$-holomorphic map for any fixed $\tau\in[0,1]$, either from the oriented sphere, or from a compact disk with its entire boundary on $L_\gamma$. Let $n_R(u)=n_{a_R}(u)$ be the actual absolute or relative divisor degree constructed by the point-divisor intersection lemma. Then every $n_R(u)$ is a nonnegative integer, and a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometry and path satisfies
$$E_g(u)\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
This includes spheres lying entirely in $\Delta$ or in a point divisor; no off-diagonal-end hypothesis is present.

For a sphere all region coefficients equal one nonnegative integer $d_0$, and $n_a(u)=d_0$ for every $a\in\Sigma$. For a one-torus disk, let $A_i$ be the connected components of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup_j\gamma_j$. Its coefficient function is constant on each $A_i$, say $b_i\ge0$, and its domain is $\sum_i b_i[A_i]$; in particular its boundary has only $\gamma$ curves. If one marked point $z_i$ is chosen in each $A_i$ away from all attaching curves, then $n_{z_i}(u)=b_i$.

Consequently a sphere with one zero point-divisor degree is constant. A one-torus disk with all the degrees $n_{z_i}$ zero is constant. The disk conclusion uses one marked point in each actual complement component, as provided by a complete marked cut system, and does not require any admissibility assertion about two-torus periodic domains or a Maslov-index formula. Applying them to a zero-mark degeneration still requires a proved additivity statement for the divisor degrees of its limiting components.

Assume Countable Choice. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$ for a closed connected Riemann surface, and fix finitely many product tori $L_j$ from systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves. Let $a\in\Sigma$ lie off all these curves. The actual point-divisor bundle of $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, with its canonical section on the boundary, defines integer degrees $n_a$ for disks and spheres, including contained spheres. It also defines an integer for every smooth strip between two transverse specified tori, with simultaneous product generator charts and uniform ends at their intersections: truncate and cap its ends inside sufficiently small generator charts avoiding $E_a$. The integer is independent of the sufficiently remote cuts and these local caps, and agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity whenever the latter is defined.

In the actual bounded-energy compactness conclusions of the bordered-source bubble-tree theorem, when the fixed source is a disk, or of the bubbled transverse-strip breaking theorem, these degrees satisfy, for all sufficiently large sequence indices,
$$n_a(u_n)=\sum_{\text{base or strip levels }v}n_a(v)+\sum_{\text{bubble components }w}n_a(w).$$
The hypotheses of those compactness theorems, including their common exact transverse generator charts for strips, are retained. No avoidance of $E_a$ by interior nodes or sphere bubbles is required. The formula holds simultaneously for any fixed finite set of such points.

In particular suppose the strip sequence satisfies that transverse-strip compactness theorem and the compact-bubble domain-energy lemma, with common diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods and uniformly bounded geometric constants. Let $z_1,\ldots,z_k$ be marked points off all attaching curves, with $J_{n,t}$ and its limit equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near their divisors. Require that each connected component of the complement of each individual boundary curve system contains at least one of these marked points. If $n_{z_i}(u_n)=0$ for every $i,n$, its limit has no nonconstant sphere or disk bubbles. In fact no bubble vertices remain after discarding redundant constant vertices, and every retained strip level is nonconstant and has $n_{z_i}=0$ for every $i$. Thus that actual compactness theorem reduces to finite breaking of unbubbled zero-marked strips, with its smooth local convergence and full energy and neck-collapse conclusions. This does not assert regularity of same-generator index-two strips, a Maslov/domain-index identity, low-index stratum dimensions, or gluing.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a smooth real rank-$2m$ vector bundle on $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, with a smooth endomorphism $J$ satisfying $J^2=-I$. On the two boundary edges let $F_0,F_1$ be smooth real rank-$m$ subbundles with $F_j\cap JF_j=0$. Suppose that outside a compact strip there are specified smooth complex frames $\tau_\pm:\mathbb C^m\to E$, intertwining $i$ and $J$, in which $F_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $F_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real linear first-order operator on sections of $E$ with symbol
$$P(f\xi)=fP\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ\xi$$
for every smooth real function $f$, and suppose its expression in each end frame is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ outside a compact strip.

There exist a global smooth complex frame $\Phi$, a sign matrix $S_+=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma,1,\ldots,1)$ with $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$, an integer $\ell$, and a smooth real function $\vartheta(s)$, constant at $\pi/2$ on the negative end and $\pi/2+\ell\pi$ on the positive end, such that $\Phi=\tau_-$ on the negative end, $\Phi=\tau_+S_+$ on the positive end, and
$$F_0=\Phi\mathbb R^m,\qquad F_1=\Phi\left(e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R^{m-1}\right).$$
In this frame $P$ is $\partial_s+i\partial_t+B(s,t)$ with smooth compactly supported real linear $B$. On the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth sections satisfying those actual boundary subbundles, with the norm defined by finite bundle charts on a compact core and the prescribed frames on the ends, $P$ maps to the corresponding $L^2(E)$ space and is real Fredholm, with
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=-\ell.$$
The same index holds with the weight $e^{\delta|s|}$ for $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. These are indices before any translation quotient. The integer $\ell$ is independent of the choices in the construction, since it is minus the index of this fixed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to the actual linearization at a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip of finite Dirichlet energy, measured in a smooth target metric, in a compact target, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of transverse finite intersection, whenever the chosen target charts at their intersections identify those submanifolds with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with the constant structure $i$ for every $t$. For product Heegaard tori such a geometric choice is available by the product-integrable generator-neighborhood construction. No domain Euler-measure formula, corner/excision theorem, generic regularity, or moduli count is part of this conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Write $X_0=H^1_\theta$ for the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $B:S\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m)$ be smooth up to the boundary, with every derivative bounded, and suppose its uniform end limits are real diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$$X_q=H^{q+1}(S;\mathbb C^m)\cap X_0,\qquad Y_q=H^q(S;\mathbb C^m),\qquad T_q=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X_q\longrightarrow Y_q,$$
using real Hilbert spaces and their indicated Sobolev norms. There are no higher boundary conditions: only the zeroth trace encoded by $X_0$ is required. In particular no normal derivative or forcing trace is prescribed.

Every $T_q$ is bounded Fredholm. Its kernel is the same set as the kernel of $T_0$, and its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}T_0$. The inclusion of $Y_q$ in $L^2$ induces an isomorphism of real cokernels. Thus
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_q=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_0=\sum_j\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
More precisely, if $u\in X_0$ and $T_0u=f\in H^q$, then $u\in X_q$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q\bigl(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr).$$

The same conclusions hold with smooth two-sided weights $w=e^{\delta\rho(s)}$, where $\rho$ is smooth, equals $|s|$ outside a compact interval, has all derivatives of positive order bounded, and $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm,j,n}|\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}|$. Weighted spaces mean $wu\in X_q$ and $wf\in Y_q$. Their index is the same displayed index. The weight is smooth at zero even for $q\ge1$.

Finally, for an actual geometric strip operator with exact product-integrable ends and the smooth bundle frame supplied by the geometric strip normal-form theorem, the actual $H^{q+1}$ boundary-section domain and $H^q$ target have this same real index before translation quotient, also with these smooth weights. This asserts integer Hilbert Sobolev agreement; no $W^{1,p}$ comparison or Heegaard-domain Euler formula is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold with a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact submanifolds totally real for $J_0,J_1$, respectively. Suppose their intersection is finite and transverse. At each intersection point choose a target chart in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Retain those same charts and structures throughout.

A smooth fixed-end representative from $x$ to $y$ is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ with boundary on $L_0,L_1$, identically $x$ on one full negative tail and identically $y$ on one full positive tail. Its covariant Cauchy–Riemann linearization on fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ spaces is Fredholm. Its real index is independent of the chosen smooth connection and of the representative under any smooth relative homotopy $H(h,s,t)$ with those boundary conditions, fixed endpoints, and one common pair of constant tails for all $h\in[0,1]$.

These indices add under concatenating two such representatives at their common endpoint, are zero for a constant representative, and change sign when $u(s,t)$ is replaced by $u(-s,t)$. Thus they define an integer index on smooth fixed-end representatives modulo the stated smooth relative homotopies, with concatenation and reversal laws. This result includes nonholomorphic representatives. It does not assume that a nonlinear moduli space exists or is regular.

A further relative smoothing and end-flattening argument is required to identify this smooth quotient with a Whitney-class set defined initially by arbitrary continuous disk maps and continuous relative homotopies. No such identification, domain Euler formula, or arbitrary-class representativity theorem is asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice. In the compact transverse geometry with common exact product generator charts, let an actual sequence of strips have the unbubbled breaking conclusion of the strip compactness theorem, with nonconstant levels $v_1,\ldots,v_M$, matched end generators and no additional energy or image diameter on the intermediate necks or outer tails. Each strip determines its continuous Whitney class by filling its two uniform generator ends, with boundary arcs on $L_0,L_1$. Concatenation joins matching constant end neighborhoods, or equivalently the corresponding marked disk ends.

For all sufficiently large $n$, the actual relative classes satisfy
$$[u_n]=[v_1]*\cdots*[v_M].$$
These are classes under continuous homotopies fixing the two marked ends and preserving each boundary arc. The conclusion uses the actual image collapse and smooth core convergence, not just equality of divisor degrees or energy. It applies in particular to the actual zero-marked unbubbled compactness conclusion, without any additional index hypothesis.

For the actual regular-pair pregluing $u_R$ and Newton-corrected strip $g_R$ in the regular-strip gluing lemma, for all sufficiently large $R$ one has
$$[g_R]=[u_R]=[u^-]*[u^+].$$
No converse classification of relative classes, Maslov/domain formula, or gluing for bubbles or degenerating targets is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $u$ be an actual smooth finite-energy strip in the compact exact-generator geometry of the actual higher Sobolev strip-chart construction, and let $P:H^1\cap\mathcal X^1\to L^2$ be its geometric Cauchy–Riemann linearization. Use any fixed smooth positive definite target metric and source measure $ds\,dt$ to define the real $L^2$ pairing. Every $\eta\in L^2$ which annihilates $\operatorname{Ran}P$ has a smooth representative on $\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. In each smooth local frame that representative satisfies the actual formal adjoint equation. For compact subsets $K\subset\operatorname{int}U$ in a coordinate patch inside the strip and every integer $q\ge0$,
$$\|\eta\|_{H^q(K)}\le C_{K,U,q}\|\eta\|_{L^2(U)},$$
where the constant depends on the indicated compact containment and finitely many local smooth coefficient and metric bounds. No boundary regularity or adjoint boundary formula is asserted.

More generally, let $K_0:H\to H^2(u^*TX)$ be any bounded linear parameter derivative from a real Hilbert space, including the actual derivative $b\mapsto(d_aJ[b])_t(u)u_t$ of the smooth Hilbert family. The operators
$$A_0(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^1\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow L^2,$$
$$A_2(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^3\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow H^2$$
both have closed range, and $A_0$ is onto if and only if $A_2$ is onto. They are onto exactly when there is no nonzero $L^2$ section $\eta$ such that
$$\langle\eta,P\xi\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }\xi\in H^1\cap\mathcal X^1,\qquad \langle\eta,K_0b\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }b\in H.$$
Each such obstruction is smooth on the interior by the first assertion. Thus actual interior unique continuation can be applied to an $L^2$ obstruction after this lemma; an $H^2$-dual distribution need not be mistaken for an $L^2$ function. The lemma does not prove unique continuation or rule out the displayed obstructions.

Assume countable choice and write $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t=2\partial_{\bar z}$ on a connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$. Let $B\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m))$, and let $v\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C^m)$, for some $p>2$, solve $Dv+Bv=0$ weakly. Use its continuous representative. Near every point $z_0$ there are a continuous invertible complex matrix $P$, belonging locally to $W^{1,q}$ for every finite $q>2$, and a holomorphic vector function $h$ with $v=Ph$. One may normalize $P(z_0)=I$.

Consequently either $v$ is identically zero, or all its zeros are isolated and have finite order: at a zero $z_0$ there are an integer $k\ge1$ and constants $c,C,r>0$ with
$$c|z-z_0|^k\le|v(z)|\le C|z-z_0|^k\qquad(0<|z-z_0|<r).$$
In particular vanishing on an open set, or vanishing to infinite order at one point, forces global vanishing. The same conclusions hold for $v_s+J(s,t)v_t+Av=0$ when $J$ is a smooth family of real complex structures and $A$ is locally bounded; the local factor is then an invertible real matrix rather than necessarily a complex matrix.

If two smooth maps solve the same equation $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$ for a smooth almost complex family on a smooth target and have matching infinite jets at one interior point, they agree everywhere on their connected common source. Agreement on an open set suffices. This assertion concerns parametrized maps and actual linear equations; it does not infer moduli transversality or an injective-point theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be compact with a fixed smooth metric, $J_t$ a smooth family of almost complex structures, and $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ a smooth nonconstant solution of
$$u_s+J_t(u)u_t=0$$
with finite Dirichlet energy and uniform limits $x_-,x_+$ as $s\to-\infty,+\infty$. Let $K\subset X$ be any finite set containing these limits. Then the set
$$\mathcal R(u)=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb R\times(0,1):u_s(s,t)\ne0,\ u(s,t)\notin K,\ u(s',t)=u(s,t)\Rightarrow s'=s\}$$
is open and dense in the interior strip.

In particular this applies to actual finite-energy strips with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of finite transverse intersection and fixed longitudinally independent boundary structures: their uniform ends exist by the transverse-end-convergence theorem. The conclusion concerns injectivity at a fixed time coordinate. It does not assert global injectivity of $u$ or ensure that a point of $\mathcal R(u)$ lies outside a prescribed closed region of allowed almost-complex perturbations.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$, and a smooth $J_t$ with fixed totally real boundary structures. Suppose fixed disjoint generator charts about their finite intersection identify the boundaries with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with $i$ for every $t$. Fix end generators $x_-,x_+$ and $0\le\delta<\pi/2$, using a smooth weight $e^{\delta\rho(s)}$ as in the weighted Sobolev algebra lemma.

There is an actual second-countable separable real Hilbert configuration manifold $\mathcal B_\delta$ of strip maps with these boundary values and ends, constructed as the union of the following local charts. A reference map $u_0$ is smooth, satisfies the boundary condition, and equals $x_\pm$ outside a compact longitudinal interval. Its tangent model is
$$\mathcal X_{u_0}=H^3_\delta(u_0^*TX)\cap\mathcal X^1_{u_0},$$
where $\mathcal X^1_{u_0}$ is the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth tangent sections satisfying $TL_0,TL_1$ on the edges. This is an intersection with the $H^1$ domain, not an asserted $H^3$ closure. Small sections give maps $u=\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)$ for the actual boundary-preserving local addition. All smooth finite-energy $J_t$ strips with these ends belong to this manifold.

The actual Cauchy–Riemann expression $u_s+J_t(u)u_t$ defines a smooth section of the Hilbert bundle with fiber $H^2_\delta(u^*TX)$. In the local-addition trivialization it is a smooth map $\mathcal F_{u_0}:\mathcal X_{u_0}\to H^2_\delta(u_0^*TX)$. On a small norm ball its nonlinear remainder obeys
$$\|\mathcal F(\xi)-\mathcal F(\eta)-D\mathcal F(0)(\xi-\eta)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C(\|\xi\|_{H^3_\delta}+\|\eta\|_{H^3_\delta})\|\xi-\eta\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$
The constants are uniform for reference families with uniform coefficient/frame derivatives through the orders used in this estimate. Every zero is smooth and has finite energy and the prescribed ends. At each zero the derivative is the actual geometric Fredholm linearization $H^3_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2_\delta$, with the same real index as its $H^1\to L^2$ realization, before translation quotient. No universal transversality or gluing is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice and put $S=\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. For $k=1,2,3$ there is a bounded linear extension $H^k(S)\to H^k(\mathbb R^2)$, using no boundary condition. The spaces have the estimates $H^1(S)\subset L^4(S)$, $H^2(S)\subset C^0(\overline S)\cap L^\infty(S)$, and $H^3(S)\subset C^1(\overline S)$, with bounded supremum norms in the last two assertions. In particular
$$\|fg\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_{H^2}\|g\|_{H^2}.$$

Fix smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ outside a compact interval, with bounded derivatives, and $\delta\ge0$. Set $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ and $\|u\|_{H^k_\delta}=\|wu\|_{H^k}$. The same embeddings hold with $w|u|$, or $w(|u|+|du|)$ for $k=3$, bounded by the weighted norm. Products satisfy
$$\|fg\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|f\|_{H^2_\delta}\|g\|_{H^2_\delta},\qquad \|du\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|u\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$

Let $h(s,t,z)$ be smooth up to the boundary for $z$ in a finite-dimensional ball about zero, with bounded mixed derivatives of source order at most two and every finite target order on smaller target balls, and $h(s,t,0)=0$. Then $u\mapsto h(s,t,u)$ is a smooth map from the open subset of $H^2_\delta$ whose supremum lies in that ball to $H^2_\delta$. Its derivatives are the ordinary pointwise derivatives of $h$. On a sufficiently small bounded norm ball the remainder $Q(u)=h(s,t,u)-h_z(s,t,0)u$ satisfies
$$\|Q(u)-Q(v)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{H^2_\delta}+\|v\|_{H^2_\delta}\bigr)\|u-v\|_{H^2_\delta}.$$
All statements hold componentwise for finite-dimensional real or complex targets.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact smooth submanifolds whose intersections are finite and transverse. Suppose fixed disjoint coordinate neighborhoods of the intersection points take both submanifolds to linear subspaces, as provided by the product generator charts. Then there is a smooth map
$$\mathcal E:\{(x,v)\in TX:|v|_g<\epsilon\}\longrightarrow X$$
for some $\epsilon>0$, with $\mathcal E(x,0)=x$, $d_v\mathcal E(x,0)=I$, and $\mathcal E(x,v)\in L_j$ whenever $x\in L_j$, $v\in T_xL_j$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto(x,\mathcal E(x,v))$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of the diagonal in $X\times X$ after shrinking its domain. Its inverse for sufficiently close pairs in $L_j\times L_j$ takes values in $TL_j$.

On smaller fixed generator neighborhoods it is exactly coordinate addition:
$$q(\mathcal E(x,v))=q(x)+dq_xv$$
for all sufficiently small $v$. Derivatives of every fixed order of this addition and its inverse are uniformly bounded on smaller neighborhoods in finite coordinate covers. This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-preserving local addition, not an assumption about a Sobolev map space.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M,N$ be Hausdorff second-countable $C^r$ manifolds modeled on separable real Hilbert spaces, and let $f:M\to N$ be $C^r$, where $r$ is a positive integer or $\infty$. Suppose every derivative $Df(x)$ is a bounded Fredholm operator of the same index $d$ and $r>\max\{d,0\}$. Then the regular values of $f$ form a dense residual subset of $N$. A value is regular if every derivative at its inverse images is surjective; values with empty inverse image are regular.

Here Hilbert completeness means convergence of Cauchy sequences. No arbitrary-index choice or dependent-choice axiom is assumed. This theorem concerns a map already known to be Fredholm; it does not establish Fredholmness of a differential operator or transversality of its universal solution space.

Assume countable choice. Let $E,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $f$ a $C^1$ map on an open neighborhood of the closed ball $\overline B_E(0,r)$, and $D=df(0)$. Suppose a specified bounded linear map $Q:Y\to E$ satisfies $DQ=I_Y$. Fix $M>0$, $L\ge0$ with $\|Q\|\le M$ and
$$\|df(x)-df(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in\overline B_E(0,r)).$$
Put $\varepsilon=\|f(0)\|$. If
$$2M\varepsilon<r,\qquad MLr\le\tfrac12,$$
then there is a unique $x\in\operatorname{im}Q\cap\overline B_E(0,r)$ with $f(x)=0$. It satisfies
$$\|x\|\le2M\varepsilon,\qquad \|x+Qf(0)\|\le2M^3L\varepsilon^2.$$
The sequence $x_0=0$,
$$x_{n+1}=-Qf(0)-Q\bigl(f(x_n)-f(0)-Dx_n\bigr)$$
converges to this correction, with contraction ratio at most $1/2$. At the corrected zero $df(x)$ is still surjective, with specified right inverse
$$Q_x=Q\bigl[I_Y+(df(x)-D)Q\bigr]^{-1},\qquad \|Q_x\|\le2M.$$

The following local smooth conclusions also hold. If $f(0)=0$, $f$ is $C^q$, $1\le q\le\infty$, and $D$ has the specified bounded right inverse $Q$, continuity of $df$ alone suffices for a local $C^q$ zero-set chart. With $K=\ker D$ and $V=\operatorname{im}Q$, there is a $C^q$ map $v$ from a neighborhood of $0$ in $K$ to $V$, with $v(0)=dv(0)=0$, such that, in a product neighborhood for $E=K\oplus V$,
$$f(k+w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=v(k).$$
For a $C^q$ family $f(p,z)$, $p$ in any Banach parameter space, the same assertion holds locally with $v=v(p,k)$ whenever $f(p_0,0)=0$ and $d_zf(p_0,0)Q=I_Y$. In particular, if $Q(p)$ is a specified $C^q$ family of right inverses to $d_zf(p,0)$ and the quantitative hypotheses hold strictly with locally uniform constants, the unique corrections in $\operatorname{im}Q(p)$ depend $C^q$ on $p$.

This is an abstract correction and chart theorem. It assumes the right inverse and all displayed estimates; it supplies no geometric pregluing, uniform right-inverse construction, Fredholm index, or gluing exhaustion theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix complete singly pointed Heegaard data of any closed oriented three-manifold, a surface complex structure $j$, protected nearly symmetric geometry and exact product generator charts. Let $J_n(s,t)$ converge smoothly with all derivatives to $J_\infty(s,t)$, with uniformly bounded coefficients in one small fixed Cayley neighborhood of that background. Suppose there are autonomous paths $J_n^\pm(t)\to J_\infty^\pm(t)$ such that $J_n(s,t)-J_n^\pm(t)$ tends to zero, with every coefficient derivative, as $s\to\pm\infty$, UNIFORMLY in $n$. This includes families which are exactly autonomous outside one common compact transition interval, and also rapidly decaying source perturbations and their compact-transition truncations.
